title: Batched Migration/Refactor with Regression Gates — Internal Practice

claims.text: Templating the first minimal exemplar as a precedent commit reduces rework rate in subsequent batches because all batch agents share a concrete verified reference.
A per-batch regression gate (compile + tests + lint + artifact diff) catches cross-batch cascading breakage before it accumulates, making total repair cost lower than detecting at the end.
Worktree isolation per batch prevents in-flight batches from interfering with each other and makes rollback atomic.
Forbidding test-assertion weakening during migration is a reliable proxy for behavior preservation when full semantic equivalence checking is impractical.

hypotheses.text: Minimal-exemplar-first + precedent commit reduces per-batch agent error rate vs. diving straight into batch execution.
Per-batch regression gate catches at least one cascading breakage that would have been missed by end-of-migration testing.
